sentences.text: The petitioners are apprehending their arrest in connection with Gumla P.S. Case No.37 of 2023 for the offences punishable under Sections 406/420/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, have prayed for grant of anticipatory bail.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners have been falsely implicated in the present case and have not committed any offence as alleged in the F.I.R.

It has been alleged that on 8th April, 2021, the petitioners along with two others came at the timber shop of the informant with a truck bearing registration no.BR-21E-2235 and made him talk on their mobile phone to one Bhuneshwar Kumar who by presenting himself as the owner of the "Mahavir Timber", Mauzipur,
near Vishakha Godown, (Fatuha, Bihar), requested the informant to send two trucks of timbers Vikash Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand .......... Opp. ... on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134355815/
1 assuring that total cost of the same would be paid together after completing delivery of the order.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thereafter, the informant firstly sent one truck timber worth Rs.2,69,423.50/- by the said truck generating forest permit number and e-way bill for the same.

Again on 14th June, 2021, the informant sent the timber worth Rs.3,48,491.40/- generating forest permit number and e-way bill through the aforesaid persons which was transported to the owner of said "Mahabir Timber" by the said truck.

Hence, the informant sent the timbers worth Rs.6,17,914.90/- to said "Mahabir Timber"
on the assurance given by the petitioners and owner-Bhuneshwar Kumar.

However, when the informant tried to contact Bhuneshwar Kumar for making payment by sending him a legal notice,
he did not reply.
3. It is further submitted that the petitioner no.1 is the owner and the petitioner no.2 is the driver of truck bearing registration no.BR-21E-2235.

On perusal of the written report, it would be evident that the timbers were purchased from the informant by co-accused-Bhuneshwar Kumar and if at all the consideration for purchased of the same was not paid by the said co-accused, he can only be said to be responsible for the same.

The informant has, however, made a false allegation that the petitioners had asked the informant to release the timbers for transportation with assurance that the said amount would be paid by co-accused-Bhuneshwar Kumar to him.
They, however, undertake to co-operate in the ongoing investigation.
Hence, they may be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.
4. Learned A.P.P. opposes the petitioners' prayer for grant of anticipatory bail.
5. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and considering the materials available on record, I am inclined to enlarge the petitioners on anticipatory bail.

Accordingly, the petitioners, above named, in the event of their arrest or surrender before the court below within three weeks from today, shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.20,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand)
each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Gumla in connection with Gumla P.S. Case No.37 of 2023, subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 482(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

(Rajesh Shankar, J.) Arpit/
